question_text: A helicopter lands $5\text{ km}$ east and $7\text{ km}$ south of its starting point.

subparts.stem: Find the helicopter's distance from its starting point.
subparts.solution:
Suppose the helicopter starts at S and lands at F.
$x^2 = 7^2 + 5^2$ {Pythagoras}
$= 74$
$x = \sqrt{74}$ $\{x > 0\}$
$\approx 8.60$

$\therefore$ the helicopter is about $8.60\text{ km}$ from its starting point.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Displacements along cardinal directions form a right-angled triangle whose hypotenuse is the straight-line distance, calculated via Pythagoras' theorem.
step_by_step: Identify the East displacement ($5\text{ km}$) and South displacement ($7\text{ km}$).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Adding the distances directly ($5 + 7 = 12$) instead of using the Pythagorean theorem.

subparts.stem: Find the helicopter's bearing from its starting point.

mark_breakdown.desc: Add $90^\circ$ to find the three-figure bearing: $144.5^\circ$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A bearing is an angle measured clockwise from true North ($000^\circ$). If the direction is south of east, add the angle from East to $90^\circ$, or subtract from $180^\circ$.
step_by_step: In the right triangle, find angle $\theta$ below East: $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{South}}{\text{East}} = \frac{7}{5}$.
Because East is at a bearing of $090^\circ$, the bearing from the starting point is $90^\circ + 54.5^\circ = 144.5^\circ$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Giving $\theta = 54.5^\circ$ as the final bearing without referencing true North.
